title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Ten Drexel study environments for silent work, group sessions, presentations, and between-class reading—with access and reservation details attached.

cards.title: Bring the Whole Project Team
cards.subtitle: Rooms for groups of four to 12
cards.notes: Each room has either a writing surface or wall-mounted monitor.
cards.short_summary: A reservable setup for collaborative writing, screen sharing, and working sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Hagerty Library has 22 group study rooms for four to 12 people, each with a writing surface or wall-mounted monitor.
cards.access_notes: Current Drexel students, faculty, and staff need University ID. Groups of at least two may reserve a room for up to three hours.

cards.title: Reserve a Silent Seat Downstairs
cards.subtitle: Individual seating in a designated silent area
cards.notes: The lower level pairs a quiet-use rule with reservable individual seats.
cards.short_summary: A defined option for solo reading, drafting, or other work that benefits from silence.
cards.evidence_claim: The lower level of Hagerty Library provides reservable individual seating in a silent study area.
cards.access_notes: Individual reservations are for Drexel community members; standard Hagerty Library entry rules apply.

cards.title: Take Silent Study Upstairs
cards.subtitle: Second-floor individual seats
cards.notes: The silent designation makes this a straightforward choice for focused solo work.
cards.short_summary: Individual seating for work that does not require conversation or group equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: Hagerty Library’s second floor includes individual seats designated for silent study.
cards.access_notes: Drexel community members may reserve seats. A valid photo ID is required for entry to Hagerty Library.

cards.title: Rehearse in the Practice Zone
cards.subtitle: A 24-hour option with booths and tables nearby
cards.notes: The surrounding Den offers booths, tables, and group-work configurations.
cards.short_summary: A named practice environment suited to work that needs rehearsal rather than silent reading.
cards.evidence_claim: The 24-hour Learning Den includes a Practice Zone among its booths, tables, and group-work options.
cards.access_notes: Available to the Drexel community. Dragon Card swipe entry is required after the main library closes.

cards.entity_name: Dragons’ Learning Den Data Visualization Zone
cards.title: Put Visual Work on Display
cards.subtitle: A group-work zone for data visualization
cards.notes: Its designated purpose distinguishes it from the Den’s general booths and tables.
cards.short_summary: A specialized environment for teams developing or reviewing visual presentations of data.
cards.evidence_claim: The Learning Den identifies a Data Visualization Zone as one of its group-work environments.
cards.access_notes: Available around the clock to the Drexel community; use a Dragon Card for entry after Hagerty Library closes.

cards.title: Book a Private Group Session
cards.subtitle: Conference space for study hours or meetings
cards.notes: Private use requires advance coordination rather than an informal claim on the room.
cards.short_summary: A defined meeting environment for a group that needs to study or confer together.
cards.evidence_claim: Main 220 includes a conference space that groups may use for study hours or meetings.
cards.access_notes: Groups and student organizations must email the Dean of Students office to reserve the conference room for private use.

cards.title: Study Above the Dining Floor
cards.subtitle: Dedicated study areas beside lounges and game rooms
cards.notes: The study areas occupy Ross Commons above its first-floor dining space.
cards.short_summary: A student-center alternative with dedicated work areas and nearby shared spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Ross Commons supplies dedicated study areas alongside lounges and game rooms.
cards.access_notes: Ross Commons is a community space for students, faculty, staff, and guests. Consult current student-center hours before visiting.

cards.title: Set Up Between Classes
cards.subtitle: Tables, chairs, couches, and kitchenette amenities
cards.notes: Tables and chairs support light study; couches and kitchenette facilities provide a place to pause between sessions.
cards.short_summary: A commuter-focused environment for lighter coursework and breaks during the day.
cards.evidence_claim: The commuter lounge’s tables and chairs support light studying, while its couches and kitchenette accommodate breaks between classes.
cards.access_notes: Drexel characterizes this as a commuter-student gathering space. Rush Building access rules apply.

cards.title: Reconfigure the Terrace
cards.subtitle: Adjustable seating and whiteboards
cards.notes: The movable setup accommodates either individual work or a group gathered around a whiteboard.
cards.short_summary: A flexible environment that can shift between solo study and collaborative problem-solving.
cards.evidence_claim: The Terrace accommodates individual or group study with adjustable seating and whiteboards.
cards.access_notes: Verify current access hours. Check whether tutoring or coaching has scheduled the private hub before planning to use it.

cards.title: Try the Tech Lounge
cards.subtitle: A technology-oriented lounge in the student-center complex
cards.notes: Drexel identifies the Tech Lounge as a distinct service and space, but does not detail its equipment.
cards.short_summary: A named technology-oriented environment worth checking when general lounge seating does not fit the task.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel lists a Tech Lounge among the services and spaces in the Creese Student Center and MacAlister Hall complex.
cards.access_notes: The source does not publish reservation rules, equipment details, or hours. Confirm access locally before relying on the space.
